requirements.evidence: All requirements are covered. Default map and range fallback: app/Models/Queue.php:141-145, 171-179. Custom map with model-level validation (canonical keys, A-Z values, effective uniqueness including uncovered 0/10/20 defaults) and empty -> null normalization in the saving hook: Queue.php:158-276. The map stays out of #[Fillable] (Queue.php:130 unchanged). issue_date migration does add nullable -> backfill DATE(issued_at) -> NOT NULL -> swap unique, with a down() (2026_10_29_000001...php:15-30). Next code is scoped by queue, day and prefix, skipping malformed codes (app/Models/Ticket.php:323-356). IssueTicket reads the clock once (IssueTicket.php:32, 51, 66-67). Factory aligns issue_date and allocates by priority and day (TicketFactory.php:416-441). UpdateQueue validates before it mutates and raises ValidationException on priority_prefix_map (UpdateQueue.php:93-104). Docs are updated. Small risks: the migration drops the (queue_id, code) unique before it adds the new one (line 509-510). On MariaDB this can fail if that index is the only one backing the queue_id FK. Also, down() re-adding (queue_id, code) will fail once daily codes repeat.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through UpdateQueue/IssueTicket. Authorization stays at Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue). $fillable is deliberately left without the map. CHANGELOG [Unreleased], business-rules.md, database-schema.md and PHPDoc are updated, and tests are in Pest. Deviation: the migration filenames 2026_10_29_000000 / 000001 have zeroed timestamps, which suggests they were hand-written rather than created with make:migration.

security.evidence: priority_prefix_map is not mass-assignable (Queue.php:130 Fillable unchanged; test 'does not mass assign the priority prefix map'). UpdateQueue still authorizes first (UpdateQueue.php:89). Input is strictly validated (regex '/^[A-Z]$/', canonical-integer key check at Queue.php:216, 260-273). preg_quote is used when building the code regex (Ticket.php:349). The change adds no new UI or Livewire surface.

tests.evidence: The new tests/Feature/TicketCodePrefixTest.php covers: defaults and range fallback; custom map and [] -> null; non-mass-assignability; a dataset of invalid maps ('-1', 'foo', '010', 'xx', duplicates, {'0':'E'}); independent prefixes and daily restart around midnight using Carbon::setTestNow; legacy/malformed codes; factory day alignment and explicit codes; UpdateQueue atomic rejection and null = unchanged. Existing IssueTicketTest expectations are migrated A -> N without being weakened. Gaps: no test that IssueTicket uses a queue's custom map (e.g. X001); no test of the 'only A001 present -> N001' case on its own; no unauthorized-actor test for the new priorityPrefixMap parameter; no migration backfill test. The factory day test is not time-frozen and depends on today != 2026-09-28.

simplicity.evidence: The implementation is mostly lean and reuses the existing nextCode loop. Speculative extras: Ticket::nextCode accepts 'int|string $priority' with a single-letter string treated as a prefix 'for callers that compute it themselves', but no such caller exists (Ticket.php:317-330). It also re-fetches the Queue with Queue::query()->find($queueId) (Ticket.php:332), even though IssueTicket already holds $lockedQueue. normalizePriorityKey's (string)(int) re-check (Queue.php:267-273) partly duplicates the canonical regex, though it does guard overflow.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and the methods are small. The comments explain intent (single clock read at IssueTicket.php:30-31; validate-before-mutate at UpdateQueue.php:91-92). The style matches sibling files. No debug output or dead code. The overloaded int|string parameter of nextCode makes its contract less obvious.

scope.evidence: Every file changed serves the task. The docs/api/totem.md example update (A012 -> P012 and the uniqueness note) is a docs-sync change required by the new code format, not an unrelated edit.

issues.explanation: The old (queue_id, code) unique is dropped before the new (queue_id, code, issue_date) unique is created; on MariaDB this fails with 'needed in a foreign key constraint' if that index backs the queue_id FK, so the new index should be added first.
down() re-adds unique(queue_id, code) after daily sequences have produced repeated codes per queue, so the rollback fails on real data and the edge case is not handled or documented.
No test issues a ticket through IssueTicket on a queue with a custom map (e.g. expecting X001), and no test covers the 'only A001 present -> N001' case or an unauthorized priorityPrefixMap update.
nextCode accepts a string prefix through the priority parameter for nonexistent callers, and it re-queries the Queue even though IssueTicket already has the locked instance.
The zeroed timestamps (000000/000001) suggest the migrations were hand-written rather than generated with php artisan make:migration, as the conventions require.
The factory day-alignment test uses the real clock and would fail if run on 2026-09-28; it should freeze time like the other date test does.

review.summary: The change adds priority-derived N/P/E prefixes, a validated per-queue priority_prefix_map (not mass-assignable, normalized on save, managed through UpdateQueue with ValidationException) and a daily per-prefix sequence backed by tickets.issue_date, with a single clock read at issuance, factory alignment, updated docs and a solid new Pest test file. It meets essentially every requirement and convention. The remaining concerns are migration index ordering and rollback robustness, a few missing test cases (custom map used at issuance, authorization), and a small speculative overload in nextCode, so I would approve with minor follow-ups.
